metadata.note: The Lake Erie, Franklin and Clarion Railroad, whose name was almost entirely aspirational: it never reached Franklin, and it never reached Lake Erie. What it actually was is a fifteen-mile short line running north-west from a Pennsylvania Railroad connection at Summerville to Clarion, the county seat, with a half-mile branch from Sutton to Heidrick. Its roots are the Pittsburgh, Summerville and Clarion Railroad, which began operating in 1904 and was leased to the Pennsylvania Southern in 1910; the LEF&C itself was formed in 1913 by consolidating the Pennsylvania Northern, the Pennsylvania Southern and the Pittsburgh, Clarion and Franklin. It began in lumber and moved on to glass sand, glass bottles, brick from the Hanley plant at Summerville and, above all, coal, reaching a peak of about 80 miles of track around 1924. As the mines closed the traffic went with them: the ICC approved abandonment in September 1992 and the last train ran in January 1993. The roadbed is a hiking path today, which is precisely why this line could be drawn accurately -- OpenStreetMap carries the right-of-way, named, as a single continuous way.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lake_Erie,_Franklin_and_Clarion_Railroad (formed 1913 as a consolidation of the Pennsylvania Northern, Pennsylvania Southern and Pittsburgh, Clarion and Franklin; the last of those came from the Pittsburgh, Summerville and Clarion, which began operation in 1904 and was leased to the Pennsylvania Southern in 1910; main line 15 miles from a Conrail connection at Summerville to Clarion with a branch from Sutton to Heidrick; 'the railroad never reached either Franklin or Lake Erie'; track peaked at about 80 miles around 1924; carried sand for glass manufacturing, glass bottles, lumber, coal including unit trains, and brick from the Hanley Brick Plant in Summerville; ICC approved abandonment Sept 17 1992 effective Nov 12 1992, operations ceased after Jan 5 1993; the roadbed became a hiking path).

https://www.american-rails.com/lef.html (Lake Erie, Franklin & Clarion Railroad 1877-1993: a small Pennsylvania short line that began in the lumber business and later handled coal, whose fate was sealed as the coal mines shuttered; roots go back to 1903 when the Pittsburgh, Summerville and Clarion Railroad started building from the Pennsylvania Railroad connection at Summerville to Clarion, about 15 miles north-west; before the LEF&C, Clarion had been served by the narrow-gauge Emlenton, Shippenville & Clarion Railroad, chartered June 1875, which reached Knox in spring 1877).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: Frequencies and speeds are estimates -- and this was essentially a freight railroad, so the headways stand in for train density rather than any advertised passenger service; no passenger service appears in the available records. Also unsourced: the build date of the Sutton-Heidrick branch, which is drawn for the whole LEF&C era; the identity of the roughly 80 miles of track the company reached at its 1924 peak, only the main line and the one branch being drawn here; and the discrepancy between american-rails, which dates the company 1877-1993 and has the Pittsburgh, Summerville and Clarion starting construction in 1903, and Wikipedia, which gives 1904 for the start of operation. The 1877 date appears to reach back to the separate narrow-gauge Emlenton, Shippenville & Clarion, which is not the same company and is not drawn here.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass API, taken directly by name rather than routed: OSM carries the entire main line as a single 688-node way named 'Lake Erie, Franklin and Clarion Railroad' (railway=abandoned), running from Summerville to Clarion, because the abandoned right-of-way is now a trail. No shortest-path search was needed and no straight-line approximation was used anywhere on this layer.
Main line: 90 points after simplification, 23.33 km (14.49 miles) against the 15 miles the sources describe -- a 0.97x match.

Sutton-Heidrick branch: taken from the unnamed railway=abandoned way adjoining the main line at Sutton, 0.75 km (0.47 miles). Its Heidrick end falls within a metre of the Heidrick place node and its Sutton end within 182 m of Sutton, which is what identifies it as the branch the sources describe.

segments.note: Formed in 1913 by consolidating the Pennsylvania Northern, the Pennsylvania Southern and the Pittsburgh, Clarion and Franklin. Despite the ambitious name the railroad never reached either Franklin or Lake Erie -- its whole main line was these 15 miles between Summerville and Clarion; frequency estimated, unsourced

Track length peaked at about 80 miles around 1924. The road carried sand for glass making, glass bottles, lumber, coal (latterly in unit trains) and brick from the Hanley Brick Plant at Summerville; frequency estimated, unsourced

As the coal mines closed, traffic dwindled. The ICC approved abandonment on Sept 17 1992 with an effective date of Nov 12 1992, and operations ceased after Jan 5 1993. The roadbed is now a hiking path -- which is how the corridor survives in OpenStreetMap and how this line could be traced; frequency estimated, unsourced
